results.title: RFC: Vendor-neutral gen_ai.* semantic convention for LLM observability â€” feedback from Phoenix/Arize team welcome Â· Arize-ai/phoenix Â· Discussion #13041 Â· GitHub
results.content: makes `trace_id` and `span_id` more important than a flat metric name. For example, hallucination or faithfulness scores only become actionable when linked back to the retrieved sources and the exact prompt/model version that produced the answer.  I would also avoid treating `error_rate` as a first-class emitted metric if possible. Emit counted events with normalized error type and status, then derive rates downstream. It keeps the convention portable across Phoenix, OpenInference, OTel collectors, and vendor dashboards without forcing every SDK to compute windows the same way. | [...] | Hi Phoenix / Arize community,  I'm proposing a vendor-neutral, OpenTelemetry-compatible semantic convention and SDK layer for standardizing LLM observability metrics, and I'd love input from practitioners and maintainers who are building and using LLM evaluation and observability tools in production.  The problem: Teams instrumenting LLM applications today face a fragmented metric landscape. Every tool â€” including Phoenix, Langfuse, OpenLLMetry, and others â€” uses slightly different names and schemas for the same signals (latency, token counts, cost, error rates). There's no shared language at the metric layer.  The proposal: A canonical `gen_ai.` metric schema built on top of OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions:    `gen_ai.latency`, `gen_ai.time_to_first_token` (histograms) [...] | `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` |   `gen_ai.eval.` Extension Pack (directly relevant to Phoenix):   | Metric | Type | Description |  ---  | `gen_ai.eval.groundedness` | Histogram | Groundedness score [0,1] | | `gen_ai.eval.faithfulness` | Histogram | Faithfulness score [0,1] | | `gen_ai.eval.relevance` | Histogram | Context relevance score [0,1] | | `gen_ai.eval.toxicity` | Histogram | Toxicity score [0,1] |   This directly addresses question #2 about quality/evaluation metrics. The eval extension pack is designed to be optional and versioned independently from core.  Also new:    `gen_ai.rag.` extension pack with retrieval latency, context recall, and context token ratio metrics  An OTel maintainer (@trask) engaged and pointed to `semantic-conventions-genai` as the right upstream venue
